instruction: Remove people; check sail, mast and wishbone boom geometry

prompts.overtaking:
Use case: precise-object-edit / scientific-educational.
Image 1 is the existing right-of-way scene to EDIT. Image 2 is the approved board-and-rig-only port/starboard diagram: use it as the reference for the windsurf board, sail and boom drawing.
Remove BOTH people completely from Image 1, including all heads, bodies, arms, hands, legs, clothing and human-shaped shadows. Restore clean board decks and water where the people were. There must be NO people, no hands, no disembodied body parts, and no human silhouettes anywhere.
Redraw/clean the two rigs carefully to be mechanically coherent, matching Image 2. Each board has exactly ONE mast attached at the universal joint near the forward center of the deck, ONE triangular lime-and-white sail with its luff on that mast, and ONE conventional wishbone boom: its two gently curved arms clamp to that same mast and converge at the same sail clew/outhaul. No extra disconnected rods, duplicate booms, fake hand-shaped clamps, crossing spars, floating sail corners or new unexplained equipment. Keep the boom visually distinct from the mast and from footstraps. Use crisp navy outlines and restrained dimensional shading, as in the approved diagram.
Preserve all board positions, noses, headings, wake direction, navy travel arrows, wind arrows, titles, tags, labels, footer wording, colors, composition, canvas dimensions and painterly turquoise water. Do not add extra boards or sails. Preserve exactly TWO boards with their rigs. Do not turn them into dinghies.
Specific geometry: both boards point horizontally RIGHT, with A behind B in the same lane. Both are on PORT tack, and their single sails are carried on the lower/downwind (starboard) side of the rightward-pointing boards, extending aft and down as in the middle-left board in Image 2. Preserve the faster-arrow length for A, all overtaking/being overtaken labels, and the exact footer.

boom_cleanup_prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / scientific-educational.
Make a careful rig-only correction to this board-and-sail diagram. NO PEOPLE OR HANDS may be added. Preserve exactly two boards, all hull positions, headings, wind arrows, directional arrows, water, labels, titles, footer text and composition.
The current short dark tubes across the BOARD DECKS do not show a proper windsurf boom. Remove those incorrect short boom-like tubes/stubs over the decks, while retaining genuine small footstraps.
For EACH rig, draw one mechanically recognizable wishbone boom ALONG THE SAIL: one clamp on the mast at approximately mid-luff height, two smooth curved arms running aft on either side of the sail, and both arms meeting together at the same CLEW (the aft corner of the triangular sail), attached by a short outhaul. The boom must visibly reach the actual aft sail corner, NOT end on the board deck. Draw its two curved arms as one coherent elongated wishbone/oval assembly, not extra disconnected bars.
Keep one mast only: it runs continuously from the universal joint on the board along the sail's luff/front edge to the sail head. The boom clamp belongs partway along that mast, not at the universal joint or at the sail head. The three sail corners must remain a single coherent triangle: head at mast tip, tack near mast foot, clew aft at the boom end. Adjust only rig details as needed for these correct connections. Keep the sail on its existing appropriate leeward side and keep all board headings unchanged.
Use thin crisp navy rig outlines, restrained 3D depth, lime-and-white sails and the same painterly style. Do not add people, substitute sailboats, add a second sail, add unexplained poles, change text or redesign the image. Prioritize an easily understood mast-to-boom-to-clew connection.
rig_reference_pass:
Use case: precise-object-edit / compositing.
Correct the TWO windsurf RIGS in Image 1 using the UPPER windward A rig in Image 2 as the mechanical construction reference. Image 1 is the edit target and all its words, board locations, board headings, arrows, water and layout must be preserved. Image 2 is a rig reference only: do not copy its labels or scene.
The upper A rig in Image 2 has a recognizable wishbone boom crossing the MIDDLE of the sail, attached halfway up its mast and reaching its aft clew. Reproduce that construction for each rig in Image 1, rotated/mirrored to the board's existing heading and tack.
Remove the erroneous boom-like tube drawn along the OUTER PERIMETER/FOOT of each triangular sail in Image 1. That outside triangular frame is not a boom. Keep thin normal sail seams and a mast along the luff. Add ONE conventional wishbone boom per rig ACROSS THE MID-SAIL, with TWO gently curved arms from the SAME mid-mast clamp to the SAME clew/outhaul, just like the upper A rig in Image 2. The head and tack of the sail are not boom attachment points.
Use the same navy line weight and lime/white sail styling as the reference. Do not add people, hands, extra sails or disconnected spars. Do not change board nose directions or tack labels. Both rigs must remain on their existing lower/downwind side. Preserve every other part of Image 1 exactly.
overtaking_rig_transfer:
Use case: precise-object-edit / compositing.
Image 1 is the overtaking diagram to EDIT. Image 2 is the corrected opposite-tacks diagram and supplies a complete board-and-rig reference.
Replace BOTH board-and-rig drawings in Image 1 with copies of the LEFT-HAND PORT-TACK board and rig from Image 2. Use that same left-hand rig construction TWICE, with both noses pointing RIGHT. This is specifically to use its correct wishbone boom, whose two curved arms cross the middle of the sail from the mid-mast clamp all the way to the same aft clew.
Preserve the left/rear A and right/leading B positions, scale and separation from Image 1. Preserve its faster arrow at A, shorter arrow at B, all wind arrows, the overtaking title, every tag, exact footer wording, and all turquoise water and page styling. Keep the full two-board composition in landscape 1536x1024.
Do NOT copy the right-hand/starboard rig from Image 2: both boards in this overtaking image must be the rightward-heading PORT rig. Do not retain the incorrect outer triangular boom frame from Image 1. Use thin navy sail edges and the single conventional wishbone across mid-sail as drawn on the left board of Image 2. No people, no hands, no extra equipment, no words changed.
